summary: Small patch in BufferingCommitLogReader (four-zero bridge) plus a test change. It sets `position` to `startMarker.position()` after the seek, only advances `position` from the file pointer when `statusTracker.shouldContinue()`, sets `position = log.maxOffset()` after the segment loop ends normally, and also sets it when the legacy end-of-segment marker is hit. I read the whole diff and the surrounding reader and `CommitLogReader.Result.isFullyRead` (`log.completed() && marker.position >= log.maxOffset()`). I applied the logic.md and boundary.md checklists from the bundle plus the analytics `### cass-logic-boundary` lens notes (they cover option lookup, CL/DC, token ranges and RF parsing and do not apply to this patch). The main fix paths hold up: the start-offset case, the zero-padding case via the end marker or loop exhaustion, and the `int` narrowing of `maxOffset`, which fits for commitlog segments. One minor regression is reported below. Not reviewed: nothing.

findings.title: Advance position when a section ends with fewer than 4 bytes left
findings.rule: Conditions/boundaries: guard on shouldContinue() skips the position update on non-end-marker early terminations
findings.problem: The new guard `if (statusTracker.shouldContinue()) position = reader.getFilePointer()` skips the update on every early termination, but only the LEGACY_END_OF_SEGMENT_MARKER branch (line ~447) now sets position itself. The `end - reader.getFilePointer() < 4` branch in readSection (around line 432) calls `requestTermination()` with no position update. This is the case where the last mutation ends less than 4 bytes before the section end. In that case `error` is set, the section loop breaks, and the post-loop `maxOffset` assignment is also skipped. `position` therefore stays at the previous section's end (or 0 or the start marker). The listener is handed a marker at that stale position, and `isFullyRead()` stays false. Before the patch the file pointer was recorded in this case, so this is a regression, although the trigger is rare (the code comment ties it to 2.1-era logs).
findings.fix: In the `< 4` bytes branch, set `this.position = (int) reader.getFilePointer()`, or `log.maxOffset()` when this is the last section, before `requestTermination()`. Alternatively, track clean end-of-section separately from the error flag and update position in both cases.
